findings.body: The downstream package fails to compile until every custom Logger implementation is changed to add FromContext.
findings.failure_mode: Existing third-party implementations no longer satisfy the interface at compile time.
findings.impact: The downstream package fails to compile until every custom Logger implementation is changed to add FromContext.
findings.root_cause: An exported interface was extended with a new required method.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the existing Logger interface source-compatible and use a separate optional contextual-logger interface with a type assertion at the call site, or provide a compatibility adapter instead of requiring all implementations to add the method.
findings.title: Do not make FromContext a mandatory method on the exported Logger interface
findings.trigger: A downstream package supplies its own implementation of pkg/plugins/log.Logger to NewLoggerMiddleware or another consumer and upgrades to this version.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line R23 adds FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger to the exported Logger interface in pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go. This is a breaking change - any external implementation of Logger must now implement this new method or compilation fails.

findings.body: The completion log is written to an inaccessible fresh TestLogger, so the injected fake still reports zero InfoLogs calls and tests cannot assert the middleware's log output.
findings.failure_mode: Tests silently lose visibility into logging performed through the newly introduced FromContext path.
findings.impact: The completion log is written to an inaccessible fresh TestLogger, so the injected fake still reports zero InfoLogs calls and tests cannot assert the middleware's log output.
findings.root_cause: The fake creates a new independent recorder for FromContext instead of preserving the recorder supplied to the component under test.
findings.suggested_fix: Have TestLogger.FromContext return f (or return a contextual wrapper sharing f's Logs storage) so calls remain observable through the injected test logger.
findings.title: Make TestLogger retain log calls made through FromContext
findings.trigger: A test injects NewTestLogger into LoggerMiddleware, enables backend request logging, and invokes a request method.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line R47 shows TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger(), creating a fresh independent recorder. Tests injecting TestLogger into LoggerMiddleware will see zero InfoLogs.Calls because logs go to the new instance, not the injected one.

findings.body: The module no longer compiles because the exported factory symbol has been removed.
findings.failure_mode: Consumers encounter a source-incompatible API removal during upgrade.
findings.impact: The module no longer compiles because the exported factory symbol has been removed.
findings.root_cause: The public middleware factory was renamed by deleting its old exported symbol rather than preserving an alias or wrapper.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a deprecated NewInstrumentationMiddleware wrapper that delegates to NewMetricsMiddleware for at least the supported compatibility window.
findings.title: Retain the exported NewInstrumentationMiddleware compatibility entry point
findings.trigger: A downstream Go module imports clientmiddleware and calls the previously exported NewInstrumentationMiddleware factory after upgrading.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch shows LEFT L78-79 deleting NewInstrumentationMiddleware and replacing with NewMetricsMiddleware at R75-76. The exported factory symbol is removed without a compatibility alias, breaking downstream callers.

<!--

Thank you for sending a pull request! Here are some tips:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contribution guide at https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

2. Ensure you include and run the appropriate tests as part of your Pull Request.

3. In a new feature or configuration option, an update to the documentation is necessary. Everything related to the documentation is under the docs folder in the root of the repository.

4. If the Pull Request is a work in progress, make use of GitHub's "Draft PR" feature and mark it as such.

5. If you can not merge your Pull Request due to a merge conflict, Rebase it. This gets it in sync with the main branch.

6. Name your PR as "<FeatureArea>: Describe your change", e.g. Alerting: Prevent race condition. If it's a fix or feature relevant for the changelog describe the user impact in the title. The PR title is used to auto-generate the changelog for issues marked with the "add to changelog" label.

7. If your PR content should be added to the What's New document for the next major or minor release, add the **add to what's new** label to your PR. Note that you should add this label to the main PR that introduces the feature; do not add this label to smaller PRs for the feature.

-->

**What is this feature?**

- Renames the `InstrumentationMiddleware` to `MetricsMiddleware`
- Moves the contextual logger from the `Instrumentation/Metrics middleware` to the `LoggerMiddleware`

**Why do we need this feature?**

Better naming and consistency.

**Who is this feature for?**

Plugins platform.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

<!--

- Automatically closes linked issue when the Pull Request is merged.

Usage: "Fixes #<issue number>", or "Fixes (paste link of issue)"

-->

Fixes #

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Please check that:
- [x] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
- [x] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [x] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/writing-guide/contribute-release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-a-whats-new-document), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/writing-guide/contribute-release-notes/) doc.

raw_findings.body: The emitted "Plugin Request Completed" event no longer includes its traceID, preventing log-to-trace correlation that the previous middleware implementation provided.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Completion logs lose a correlation field for traced plugin requests.
raw_findings.impact: The emitted "Plugin Request Completed" event no longer includes its traceID, preventing log-to-trace correlation that the previous middleware implementation provided.
raw_findings.root_cause: The refactor removed the only explicit traceID extraction from LoggerMiddleware without adding traceID to the contextual attributes installed by the new middleware.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Restore the explicit TraceIDFromContext extraction and append the traceID to logParams when present, or ensure the contextual logger middleware adds the same traceID attribute before LoggerMiddleware logs.
raw_findings.title: Preserve trace IDs in plugin completion logs
raw_findings.trigger: A traced QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, or CollectMetrics request completes while backend-request logging is enabled.
